In this study, our primary focus is on the generation of patent abstracts and claims. ... We selected two tasks targeting distinct generation content formats: one for abstracts (Claims2Abstract) and another for next‑claim generation.
In our study, we focus on evaluating and understanding the quality of patent text generation by various language models.

Using all our human annotations from pairwise comparisons across two tasks, we assess the metrics' performance. We apply these metrics to the same sets of input and output that human annotators reviewed in pairwise comparisons.

We employed SemSim, Terms Coverage, N‑grams Coverage, FactGraph, QAFactEval, EntityGrid, and a rule‑based checker to assess the generated outputs. ... Kendall’s tau correlation was used to evaluate how well these metrics align with human judgments.
Reflecting on our analyses, we explored different evaluation metrics for two patent generation tasks.

The annotation process involved two primary annotators: a seasoned patent lawyer with over 15 years of experience in relevant domains, and a PhD student. In cases of disagreement, a third expert was consulted to reach consensus.

The annotation process involved two primary annotators: a seasoned patent lawyer with over 15 years of experience in relevant domains, and a PhD student. In cases of disagreement, a third expert was consulted to reach consensus.
guideline: Annotators were presented with paired outputs (model vs. model or model vs. human) and tasked with selecting the preferred output. They were also instructed to identify errors using detailed typologies based on issues observed in outputs.
Annotators were asked to choose the preferred generated text in a pairwise comparison and to record any errors observed, based on a detailed typology of error categories.

Annotators were presented with two types of paired outputs for each input claim or set of claims: 1. A comparison between two different models; 2. A juxtaposition of a model's output against the original abstract or subsequent claim. Annotators were also instructed to identify any errors present in the outputs using detailed descriptions and examples of possible error types.
criteria: error identification (grammatical errors, punctuation errors, formatting errors, dependency errors, clarity errors, brevity errors, content relevance errors, effectiveness errors)
